sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports are authoritative. This file stores a compact analytical snapshot and selected Power Stack-relevant observations, not a reconstructed ISM index database or confidential survey submissions.

industryRead.notableDetail: Electrical Equipment and Computer & Electronic Products reported higher new orders; both also reported higher prices, slower supplier deliveries and customers' inventories that were too low. Computer & Electronic Products also reported higher production, employment and backlog.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Manufacturing demand is not merely holding up; orders, production, employment and backlog all strengthened. The strongest direct Power Stack confirmation is the combination of electrical/electronics growth with too-low customer inventories and persistent component scarcity. Prices at 71.1 and slower deliveries mean supplier pricing power remains valuable, while low-margin contractors face input and schedule risk.

industryRead.commentRead: Construction remained in expansion and reported higher new orders and employment, but selected public commentary also highlighted mounting cost pressure. This supports infrastructure demand without assuming every contractor converts demand into margin.

services.powerStackInterpretation: Services demand remains resilient but expensive. Business Activity and New Orders accelerated while Prices rose above 70 and employment contracted. Switchgear, transformers, wire/cable and technical labour remain bottlenecks, directly supporting the grid/electrical thesis while increasing execution risk for labour- and freight-heavy construction names.

respondentCommentReview.scope: Only ISM-selected public respondent comments and aggregate diffusion data were reviewed.
respondentCommentReview.finding: Re-verified Aug 25. July remains the latest official Manufacturing and Services dataset; ISM's calendar confirms August data are not due until Sep 1 and Sep 3. Existing aggregate/selected-comment evidence continues to support the physical bottleneck framework: Electrical Equipment and Computer & Electronic Products expanded, customers' inventories were too low, and memory/semiconductors/electrical components remained scarce; services separately flags switchgear/transformer/wire-cable pressure.
respondentCommentReview.conclusion: The official July reports reinforce the physical-bottleneck framework but do not justify claiming direct respondent evidence on specific hyperscalers, transformer OEMs or individual data-centre projects.

combinedRead: July ISM remains bullish for Power Stack physical demand but not for disinflation: manufacturing re-accelerated sharply and services demand stayed firm, while prices, supplier delays and scarce electrical/electronic inputs remained elevated. Prefer backlog-rich equipment, generation, grid, cable, water and first-wave automation suppliers with pricing power over low-margin contractors and long-duration concept equities.
rawSubmissionNote: ISM does not publish the confidential individual survey submission database. Only aggregate diffusion data and selected respondent comments are public; Power Stack does not claim access to raw panel submissions.
